steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Income inequality: the top 20% earn over 5 times more than the bottom 20%. Causes: education/skills gaps, wage differentials, inheritance, and unemployment.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Wealth inequality is even greater than income inequality — wealth (assets, property) is more concentrated than income (earnings).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Consequences: poorer health and education outcomes for low-income groups, social tension, reduced social mobility, and lower aggregate demand.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Government redistribution: progressive taxation (higher earners pay more), welfare benefits (universal credit, pensions), and public services (free NHS, education).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain two causes of income inequality in the UK. | Describe how government can redistribute income through taxation and spending. | Evaluate whether reducing income inequality should be a government priority.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always distinguish INCOME (earnings per period) from WEALTH (total assets). Wealth inequality is always greater. Redistribution uses BOTH taxation (taking from rich) AND spending (giving to poor). Balance of payments deficit = imports exceed exports of goods and services.
